profiles.name: Anthony Battle
profiles.executiveSummary: Role & Background: Anthony "Tony" Battle serves as Group Chief Digital and Information Officer at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) since early 2022 1 . In this capacity, he leads JLR's global IT and digital strategy, driving the company's ambitious Digital 2024 transformation program - a core pillar of JLR's Reimagine strategy to reinvent itself as an electric-first, tech-forward luxury automaker 1 .
coreMotivations: Achieving goals
Speed & efficiency
Producing results
Independence

"Our business transformation is 100% underpinned by a digital transformation," Anthony notes, underscoring that every aspect of JLR's reinvention - from engineering to customer experience - relies on new digital capabilities 8
Pace of Change & Stakeholders: The automotive sector is evolving rapidly (electrification, Industry 4.0, direct-to-consumer models), and JLR's competitiveness hinges on speed and innovation

The operating context also includes external challenges like supply chain volatility and regulatory changes (for instance, he has cited how Brexit's new bureaucracy spurred JLR to double down on intelligent automation solutions to maintain efficiency 12 )
When others speak, he nods and asks clarifying questions, signaling that he values insight and data behind opinions
decisionHeuristics: Risk Appetite: Anthony's decision-making reflects a balanced risk appetite
Having led IT in safety-critical industries, he is vigilant about risks (cybersecurity, operational downtime, data breaches), and he institutes controls to mitigate them
He is not reckless; for example, he tempered the rush into generative AI with a pause for governance 17 , illustrating his instinct to de-risk innovations before scaling
In board settings, he often asks "What are the failure modes?" or "Have we thought through the worst-case scenario?" for new initiatives, demonstrating his proactive risk management
That said, Anthony is not risk-averse - he's comfortable taking calculated risks to drive progress
He will advocate for investment in a new technology or process if the upside is compelling and the risks can be managed
Essentially, he seeks a risk/reward sweet spot, where bold moves are backed by contingency plans and sound analysis
Innovation & Agility: Anthony is pro-innovation and pushes for agility in decision-making and execution

- Misalignment with Strategy: Anthony is quick to spot when ideas don't align with the agreed vision or strategy
If a discussion veers into initiatives that conflict with JLR's Reimagine objectives or a board's collective goals, he will challenge the group to consider alignment
5 When He Supports: On the other hand, Anthony readily voices support when he sees ideas and behaviors that drive the organization forward in line with his values

Triggers for his support include: - Strategic Alignment & Value: If someone proposes an initiative clearly linked to strategic objectives (growth, customer experience, efficiency) with tangible value, Anthony will be one of the first to nod in agreement
This encouragement helps build momentum for wellaligned proposals
- Insightful Analysis: Anthony appreciates when a colleague brings a data-driven insight or a fresh perspective to the table

profiles.name: Constantin Beier
profiles.executiveSummary: [[Person - Constantin Beier]] is the Chief Operating Officer of Aon's Strategy & Technology Group and a member of Aon's Executive Leadership Team 1 . He brings over two decades of international experience spanning enterprise risk management, data analytics, global operations, and legal expertise 2 .
coreMotivations: Renowned for integrating consulting, analytics, and technology solutions to drive business growth and improve risk outcomes, he has held multiple leadership roles at Aon - including Global Chief Data Officer - where he helped deliver data-driven solutions that enabled clients to make better decisions 3

Constantin is respected for his forward-looking yet responsible leadership style and innovation mindset, evidenced by his work building Aon's global analytics capabilities and architecting the firm's post-Brexit operating model 4

(GET TO KNOW ME: Outside work, Constantin is an avid outdoorsman - he enjoys tennis, golf, skiing, biking, and running - and he's always exploring new podcasts and audiobooks to fuel continuous learning.) Operating Context In his role at Aon, Constantin operates at the intersection of global business strategy, technology innovation, and operational excellence

He leads worldwide operations that implement Aon's data/technology strategy - managing portfolios of innovation projects and scaling analytics-driven products - all while ensuring these solutions are practical and secure for enterprise use 3 7
In short, Constantin's operating context is defined by global scale, datadriven transformation, and a commitment to innovation tempered by practical governance
Because he has earned trust through his responsible leadership, when Constantin voices a concern or an alternate idea, others listen
decisionHeuristics: Constantin's decision-making posture is characterized by a bias for rigor and strategic alignment, balanced with an openness to experimentation under controlled conditions
As a trained lawyer and veteran data executive, his instinct is to dig into the evidence: he prefers decisions to be backed by solid analysis, clear metrics, and an understanding of risks
For example, if confronted with a proposal to invest in a new AI tool, Constantin will evaluate its business case, data requirements, and risk implications in detail before supporting it
He brings a natural sense of control to decision-making - setting up frameworks or criteria to guide choices (much as he has done with innovation portfolio governance in his work 12 3 )
He often advocates pilot programs or "funnel tests" (iterative checkpoints) to try new ideas quickly and learn from them, rather than either blindly betting big or doing nothing
He frequently looks for ways to involve the right stakeholders or external partners in a decision, believing that collaborative approaches yield better outcomes

Whether it's partnering with a fintech firm for a proof-ofconcept or assembling a cross-functional team internally, his decisions lean on the idea that diverse input and shared ownership improve success

In summary, Constantin's decision posture is methodical but progressive - he insists on thorough analysis and risk assessment, yet once a path is validated, he drives execution with urgency and cooperative spirit
supportTriggers: - When He Challenges: Constantin will raise challenges in a discussion if he detects insufficient data or analysis behind an idea
He has little patience for decisions based on gut feel alone; if a proposal lacks evidence or a clear rationale, he'll likely question it (e.g., "What data do we have to support this assumption?")

Additionally, Constantin may challenge ideas that remain too siloed or narrow: if a suggestion doesn't consider cross-departmental implications or doesn't align with the broader strategy, he'll bring that up
- When He Supports: Constantin is an enthusiastic supporter of initiatives that clearly align with strategic goals and are backed by analysis
If an idea comes with compelling data, client insights, or pilot results demonstrating its value, he will readily advocate for it

He often voices support for innovative solutions that address unmet needs, especially when they are approached in a responsible, well-planned way (for example, a proposal to modernize a process using AI, accompanied by a solid implementation plan and governance measures, would gain his quick 3 endorsement)

Constantin also responds positively to collaborative approaches: if an initiative involves partnership across industries or departments, or learning from external best practices, he sees that as a plus and will support it as a means to broaden the organization's horizons
challengeTriggers: - When He Challenges: Constantin will raise challenges in a discussion if he detects insufficient data or analysis behind an idea
He has little patience for decisions based on gut feel alone; if a proposal lacks evidence or a clear rationale, he'll likely question it (e.g., "What data do we have to support this assumption?")
He is also quick to challenge when he spots risk blind-spots - for instance, if enthusiastic plans ignore potential downsides, regulatory constraints, or operational impacts

Additionally, Constantin may challenge ideas that remain too siloed or narrow: if a suggestion doesn't consider cross-departmental implications or doesn't align with the broader strategy, he'll bring that up

Finally, he is known to intervene if groupthink is in play - he'll politely offer an alternate perspective or probing question to ensure the board explores all angles rather than rubber-stamping a consensus

He strongly favors efforts that improve risk management, data capabilities, or operational efficiency, as these play to his core expertise - he'll champion investments in better analytics infrastructure or risk modeling improvements that he believes will strengthen the business long-term 3
In essence, he's inclined to support proposals that are thoughtful, evidence-based, and promise innovative growth while managing risk
languagePatternsToUse: Some examples of things you might hear him say: - "From a risk perspective, what data are we using to support this decision?" - Emphasizing the need for data-driven rationale and considering risk implications
- "Let's double-click on those numbers - what are they telling us about the trend?" - Inviting a closer analysis of data or metrics presented, to ensure understanding of underlying trends
- "How do we balance this initiative's short-term gains against long-term strategic goals?" - A question he might pose to ensure strategic alignment and sustainability 13
- "Have we thought about the governance and controls we'll need if we proceed with this?" - Underscoring his focus on responsible execution (especially for tech/AI projects)
- "Who else can we partner with to make this a success?" - Reflecting his collaborative mindset, looking for alliances or cross-functional support
- "I appreciate the idea - maybe we can run a quick pilot and gather some data before scaling up." - Encouraging experimentation but in a measured, data-gathering way
- "What's the client impact here?
Are we solving a real pain point?" - Bringing the discussion back to client value and practical impact, a perspective he often champions

profiles.name: Dave Williams
profiles.executiveSummary: [[Person - Dave Williams]] is the President of Slalom's UK & Ireland business, a position he has held since April 2017 1 . In this role, he leads Slalom's consulting operations across London, Manchester, and Dublin, driving strategy, client delivery, and sustainable growth in the region 1 . Dave joined Slalom after a 20+ year career at Accenture, where he held senior leadership roles such as Industry Managing Director for Energy (UK & Ireland) 1 .
coreMotivations: Under his leadership, Slalom UK&I has become recognized for its inclusive culture and long-term client partnerships, aligning with Dave's belief that trust and relationships are foundational to lasting success
Demand for digital transformation is high across industries, and clients expect both innovation and tangible outcomes
1 Strategic Differentiation: In this context, Dave's strategy has been to differentiate Slalom as a purposedriven, customer-obsessed, and employee-empowered partner 5
He positions Slalom UK&I as a firm that delivers business outcomes and technology solutions together - breaking down the silos between strategy and tech execution

He often highlights a vision for Slalom to be the most "customer-obsessed and employee-empowered" consultancy in the market, and this shapes decisions on what projects to pursue and how to invest for growth 5
This networked approach allows him to navigate ambiguity in the market with optimism and grounded insight: he stays attuned to global innovations while tailoring solutions to regional needs
decisionHeuristics: Dave's decision-making posture as a leader is defined by balanced boldness
He combines an appetite for innovation and smart risk-taking with a methodical, safeguards-in-place approach
Several dimensions characterize how Dave evaluates decisions: - Risk Appetite - Calculated, Not Reckless: Dave can be described as a calculated risk-taker
Having led large, mission-critical projects in his career, he is highly aware of various risks (delivery risks, security risks, market risks) and proactively manages them
He believes in derisking through preparation rather than avoiding risk outright
That said, Dave is not risk-averse - if the potential upside is compelling and risks are understood, he will support moving forward

For example, when Slalom UK considered investing heavily in a new AI partnership (a risky allocation of resources), Dave saw that the upside of market leadership outweighed the risks if executed with the right expertise

He likely said yes to Slalom becoming the first strategic partner for Salesforce's Einstein AI platform knowing it was new (uncertain), but confident in his team's abilities to deliver (mitigating the risk) 27 28
supportTriggers: In board or executive discussions, Dave has clear triggers that prompt him to challenge an idea versus actively support it

Understanding these triggers gives insight into his priorities and values: When He Challenges: Dave will raise concerns or push back if he senses an initiative is off-track, insufficiently thought out, or misaligned
His gentle questioning in these cases often elevates the conversation, prompting others to firm up their analysis or acknowledge areas of uncertainty
- Misalignment with Purpose or Strategy: Dave is quick to spot when a proposal doesn't fit the organization's core mission or agreed strategy
If an idea seems like a detour from Slalom's values or vision, Dave will ask pointedly, "Help me understand how this aligns with our purpose and strategy?" 36
This trigger helps prevent waste and promote unity - reflecting his alignment-focused leadership style
When He Supports: On the flip side, Dave is quick to voice support and become an advocate for ideas that resonate with his goals and values
challengeTriggers: In board or executive discussions, Dave has clear triggers that prompt him to challenge an idea versus actively support it

Understanding these triggers gives insight into his priorities and values: When He Challenges: Dave will raise concerns or push back if he senses an initiative is off-track, insufficiently thought out, or misaligned
Key triggers for him to challenge include: - Lack of Data or Insight: If a recommendation is presented without evidence or a solid rationale, Dave is likely to question it
His gentle questioning in these cases often elevates the conversation, prompting others to firm up their analysis or acknowledge areas of uncertainty
- Misalignment with Purpose or Strategy: Dave is quick to spot when a proposal doesn't fit the organization's core mission or agreed strategy
One of his personal principles is "purpose before profit," and he will challenge ideas that sacrifice long-term purpose for short-term gain 35
For instance, if the board discussion veers into pursuing a trendy market opportunity that doesn't play to Slalom's strengths or clients' needs, Dave would question the strategic fit
languagePatternsToUse: Some notable characteristics of his boardroom language: - Emphasis on Purpose and Values: Dave frequently reiterates the importance of purpose, culture, and "doing the right thing." A signature phrase of his is "purpose before profit," which he brings up to underline values-driven decisions 43

For example, in a strategy debate he might remind everyone, "Our guiding principle is purpose before profit - any plan we pursue should honor that." He also invokes Slalom's own motto, talking about a "fiercely human approach" to stress keeping things people-centric and real

10 - Customer-Centric Talk: Being very client-focused, Dave's contributions often include phrases about delighting customers or being "customer-centric." He might say, "Being customer-centric is what Slalom is all about," to ground a conversation back to what benefits the client 44

Common in his vocabulary are phrases like "delight our clients" or "create amazing customer experiences." For instance, if evaluating a proposal, Dave will ask, "How will this help us delight our customers?" - reframing the discussion in terms of client impact 45
It's very much Dave's style to anchor even technical or internal topics in the context of How will this ultimately help our customers?

For example, in discussing an operational change he might say, "The outcome we're aiming for is a faster turnaround - say from 4 weeks to 2 weeks - for client deliverables." He loves using specifics and metrics: you'll hear him reference "a 10% increase in productivity" or "500 team members and counting" or cite an industry stat like "84% of organizations… trust AI" to bolster a point 46 47
He essentially answers the unspoken "So what does this do for us (or our clients)?" in every statement - articulating the why and the impact, not just the what

In a board meeting with non-technical members, if AI comes up, Dave might say, "In plain terms, this AI will comb through our data and highlight patterns - essentially a smart assistant for our teams." 48 He avoids unnecessary jargon and acronyms unless the audience is deeply technical, and even then he'll clarify meaning

As he puts it, "Exercise is my release, family is my reason and work and people are my purpose and motivation" 6 , underscoring the personal values that fuel his professional life

He is tasked with continually modernizing legacy practices through innovation - leveraging artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud platforms - while maintaining trust, security and ethical standards that are paramount in risk management

He's also known to ask provocative, insight-seeking questions in a friendly manner, like "What's the worst that could happen if we don't change?" or "Is this truly solving the customer's problem or just ours?" - these prompt reflection without alienating colleagues
Yet, he remains strategic in phrasing, often re-centering the discussion: "At the end of the day, what's the outcome we want?" is a common refrain to cut through tangents and noise 2
He also speaks the language of both business and tech fluently - one moment citing growth numbers or market trends, the next moment simplifying a tech concept with an everyday analogy
In summary, Vivek's boardroom language is approachable, insightful, and catalytic - expect metaphors that clarify, questions that challenge, and phrasing that unites the team towards action
languagePatternsToAvoid: Avoid generic or boilerplate phrasing that could apply to any board member
Avoid repeating previous speaker wording unless explicitly challenging or endorsing it
Avoid vague recommendations without owner, timeline, and checkpoint
Avoid communication drainers: Following inflexible rules
Avoid communication drainers: Slow pace of work
